decision: Sparse multi-label tagging (rare labels, abstract meanings) is named as a weak spot: before relying on Jev for it, label 50 or more items for reference, with several known positives per label, and compare exact label sets and per-label hits; a 10-item pilot cannot show the weakness.

evidence.text: Pilot of 60 rules (title and one-line summary) plus 5 controls, 25 noul questions, threshold 0.5, against model reference labels: Jev 38/60 exact sets, 14/24 reference labels; a model on the same text 57/60, 21/24. Threshold sweep recomputed from the rows: 0.2 gives 31/60 exact, 19/24 found, 31 wrong extras; 0.5 gives 16 extras. RED probes (opus, haiku) on the old text answered NONE on sparse multi-label fit; GREEN probes quoted the new bullet and kept a 30 percent single-noul control out of it.

reopen_if: A Jev release, or a different state shape, reaches the model reference on a sparse multi-label pilot (exact sets and per-label hits within a few items of it).
why: One noul per label over a 25-label closed list missed many labels in a pre-registered pilot that a model given the same text found, and the 10-item pilot had looked plausible. Readers of the old text checked only the 10-item pilot's known yes and no.

why: In the same pilot every one of the 10 FLAT label questions had 0 or 1 positives in the 65-item sample, so the flat reading said nothing about the wording; the old step 5 named 'shown the items really are alike' with no method, and both probe tiers reported that gap.
